findings: Mapped summary lines 13–49 faithfully preserve the broad April UI choices and API purposes. November offers clearer selection guidance, including the Payment Sheet recommendation and effort scores 2/5, 3/5 and 3/5, same appearance controls for Flow Controller, and Payment Element inline or dedicated placement with row customizations and a detail sheet where needed (old raw lines 17–45; new raw lines 25–82). A brief locator to the nine UI/use-case links makes setup vs pay vs pay-and-save findable without duplicating the tables.

The source at lines 13–23 omits the dated US digital-goods callout and the new tap-to-add private-preview route. Route Payment Sheet and Payment Element separately. The separately captured preview guides require requesting access, an existing relevant Sheet or Element integration, a physical card and compatible NFC-equipped Android device. The server retrieves the Customer, creates a Customer-bound SetupIntent for card_present and returns its client secret to the app. Preserve the Endive version warning for the request syntax and keep general mobile SDK support separate from feature entitlement (old raw lines 4–15, new raw lines 5–23, raw/stripe-payments-mobile-tap-to-add-2026-11-07.md:9-35,71-105 and raw/stripe-payments-mobile-embedded-tap-to-add-2026-11-07.md:9-35,71-105).

The source at lines 27–61 needs to distinguish intended immediate charge, no-charge setup, and payment result. The April pay-and-save example has the server create a PaymentIntent with setup_future_usage for a customer-configured Account or Customer and a CustomerSession for temporary scoped SDK access, returning the two client secrets. Its no-charge counterpart has the server create a SetupIntent with the Customer ID and return the SetupIntent client secret. The guide describes a Customer Ephemeral Key as optional temporary access and shows it in the sample handoff. It separately directs Accounts v2 integrations to corresponding Account references (raw/stripe-inapp-save-during-payment-2025.md:115-130 and raw/stripe-inapp-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:110-131). The embedded example can return a completed client result for delayed methods while the payment is pending. Server events distinguish processing, succeeded and payment_failed and guide fulfillment (raw/stripe-inapp-save-during-payment-2025.md:620-640 and raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:747-759,905-929).

Mapped lines 53–69 retain the card/US bank/SEPA saved-method groups and CustomerSession controls. Add dated consent, method count, native wallet and payment-method eligibility qualifications and preserve both raw dates.

The mapped overview’s summary/UI sections at lines 13–23 and feature list at lines 63–69 omit the native flow both captures describe. Stripe can dynamically display 40+ methods alongside eligible saved methods, collect payment and billing details, and handle 3DS2 authentication or redirect to a banking app as applicable. This is an April/November baseline, and authentication or a browser/app return alone is distinct from final payment success (old raw lines 11–15, new raw lines 19–23).
conflicts: Platform and preview warning for the acceptance source and reciprocal wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md:10,79–84,92. New raw lines 9–17 put an unqualified all-supported-platforms sentence between the US digital-goods note and private preview. The two separate November feature guides identify Android only, a physical card and a compatible NFC device, existing Sheet or Element integration, a preview request, and server-created Customer-associated SetupIntent with card_present and client-secret handoff (raw/stripe-payments-mobile-tap-to-add-2026-11-07.md:9-35,71-105 and raw/stripe-payments-mobile-embedded-tap-to-add-2026-11-07.md:9-35,71-105). Do not attribute the broader platform sentence to private preview access. US digital-goods note remains dated and routes iOS to an app-to-web Checkout example, separate from native mobile integration. The April child demonstrates US storefront and device checks (raw/stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checkout-2025.md:1-16,339-365). No app-store policy or merchant entitlement follows from the overview.

Qualification for the retained child card_present examples. Both captured tap-to-add child snippets set payment_method_types: ['card_present'] on SetupIntent create (child raw lines 78–98). The versioned 2026-09-30.endive REST change rejects payment_method_types as a writable create field with HTTP 400 and preserves it as a computed readable property. Its Impact version wording says 2026-08-26.preview while its endpoint links and REST table identify Endive (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-36). The card-present changelog identifies allowed_payment_method_types card_present on the Endive SetupIntent create endpoint (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-card-present-and-interac-present-enum-values-for-allowed-payment-method-types-2026-11-07.md:5-28). Keep this API-version boundary next to the dated child example if reproduced, without inferring preview enablement or enrollment from the enum support.

Consent, redisplay and reusable-method warning for source lines 27–61 and reciprocal wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md:28–67,92. Both overviews describe automatic consent collection and claim global compliance (old 81–92; new 219–243). The dated mobile save-during-payment guide explicitly assigns compliance, specific-use consent, and records to the merchant and scopes redisplay via allow_redisplay (raw/stripe-inapp-save-during-payment-2025.md:22-33,115-130,634-640). CustomerSession settings control visibility, and the dated embedded saved-card flow uses payment_method_save: enabled for the checkbox (raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:794-828). Session access and the checkbox do not certify compliance or guarantee attachment/redisplay.

Source lines 42–49 say the global setup_future_usage approach disables BNPLs. Both overviews say global future usage excludes one-time methods such as most BNPLs, while method-specific setup enables a mix of one-time and reusable methods. The April narrower mobile Payment Element guide says its setup_future_usage route supports cards and US bank accounts (raw/stripe-inapp-save-during-payment-2025.md:109-130), and the dated per-method SDK preview directs the server to leave both PaymentIntent future-use fields unset while SDK IntentConfiguration supplies them (raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:3320-3354). Keep the generic example and qualify the distinct preview in source and concept (old 71–79; new 116–127,161–172,206–217; wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md:42–54).

Source lines 65–69 and concept lines 79–82 need scope. Both captures give 40+ dynamically displayed methods and a separate 100+ feature/catalog figure (old 11–15,94–105 and new 19–23,245–279). Preserve both without inferring 100+ methods show to every buyer. The overviews' wallet footnote points to a web Elements/embedded Checkout domain-registration guide (raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-pmd-registration-2026-11-07.md:5-14 and raw/stripe-pmd-registration-2025.md:4-23). Native Apple Pay configuration has a Merchant ID/certificate and Xcode capability, and Android Google Pay has native API and SDK configuration (raw/stripe-inapp-save-during-payment-2025.md:736-767,1685-1720). Do not use the overview footnote as universal native wallet registration instructions.

The overview’s merchant-controlled confirmation describes the standard Flow Controller/Payment Element pattern. The April embedded guide additionally documents native iOS default Continue and optional formSheetAction confirmation (new 25–35,65–75; raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:98-106,579-601). Keep the exception scoped in the concept and acceptance route so the default pattern does not rule out in-sheet completion for every embedded configuration.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-payments-overview-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-payments-overview.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile, new raw lines 5-23 describe native iOS, Android and React Native checkout. Both captures describe dynamic display of 40+ payment methods alongside eligible saved methods, collection of payment and billing details, and 3DS2 authentication or banking-app redirects as applicable (old raw lines 11-15, new raw lines 19-23). November adds an access-request route for the private preview of tap to add your card. The separate preview guides require requesting access, a compatible NFC Android device, a physical card and an existing Payment Sheet or Payment Element integration. The server retrieves the Customer, creates a Customer-bound card_present SetupIntent and returns its client secret for the client SDK (raw/stripe-payments-mobile-tap-to-add-2026-11-07.md:9-35,71-105 and raw/stripe-payments-mobile-embedded-tap-to-add-2026-11-07.md:9-35,71-105). The overview recommends the all-in-one Payment Sheet, gives the app confirmation control in Flow Controller, and describes embeddable method rows with Payment Element (new raw lines 25-82). The two Intent types support charging, reusable-method setup without a charge, and paying while setting future usage. The overview distinguishes global future usage, which excludes one-time methods such as most BNPLs, from method-specific future usage that can retain both categories. CustomerSession controls the consent box, display and removal of eligible saved card, US bank and SEPA methods (new raw lines 86-243). The April pay-and-save guide creates a PaymentIntent with setup_future_usage and a scoped CustomerSession for a customer-configured Account or Customer. The separate no-charge guide creates a Customer-bound SetupIntent on the server and describes an optional Customer Ephemeral Key for temporary access. The server-side events distinguish processing, succeeded and failed from client completion (raw/stripe-inapp-save-during-payment-2025.md:115-130,620-640 and raw/stripe-inapp-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:110-131). The April overview already explained the core native flow, UI and Intent choices (old raw lines 17-45, old raw lines 47-92). source-stripe-inapp-payments-overview.md reflects those UI and Intent choices but omits the native authentication path at lines 13–23 and 63–69, the preview prerequisites, and the dated trust-boundary distinctions.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile, the private-preview access disclosure is substantive; App Clip demos, illustrations, numeric complexity labels, repeated API tables and concrete links across the three UIs expand presentation and navigation. The US digital-goods note stays dated, with Android in-app and an iOS app-to-web Checkout route; further app-store or merchant eligibility requires its own evidence. The unqualified platform sentence cannot broaden the linked Android-only NFC preview (new raw lines 9-17, new raw lines 25-82, new raw lines 86-217). Preserve the old UI, API and saved-method baseline (old raw lines 17-45, old raw lines 47-92). Qualify source-stripe-inapp-payments-overview.md and its reciprocal In-App Payments concept route. The mobile save checkbox visibility depends on applicable settings and merchant responsibility for consent and redisplay remains. Global future usage excludes one-time methods such as most BNPLs, with dated mobile-specific limits and a separate SDK preview in which the SDK supplies per-method settings from IntentConfiguration rather than the server setting the fields (raw/stripe-inapp-save-during-payment-2025.md:22-33,115-130,634-640 and raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:3320-3354).
